text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 0.17% today to $458.48, continuing a sharp four-day decline that has erased most of the stock's gains from earlier this month. The selloff comes despite oil prices hitting six-month highs—Brent crude topped $116 on rising Middle East tensions and threats of U.S. strikes on Iran—which would normally lift refiner margins. The disconnect suggests investors are pricing in a risk that refiners face when geopolitical conflict disrupts global supply: tighter crude availability and potentially lower processing volumes, which can compress the profit margin refiners earn between the cost of raw oil and the price of finished fuel.

The timing also matters. U.S. refineries are running at 93.4% capacity with substantial crude and product inventories on hand, leaving little room to capitalize on higher oil prices through higher throughput. If Middle East tensions escalate into actual supply disruptions, refiners could face a squeeze where crude costs spike but they can't run plants much harder to offset it—a dynamic that has historically pressured refiner stocks even when headline oil prices look strong.
